title: Understanding Bias and Variance
text: Bias refers to the error introduced by approximating a real-world problem, which may be complex, by a simplified model. Variance refers to the model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training set. Consider how adding random noise might affect these aspects.

title: Effect of Random Features
text: Adding a feature of random numbers between $$0$$ and $$1$$ introduces noise. Think about how noise affects the model's ability to generalize from the training data to unseen data.

title: Impact on Bias
text: Does adding random noise to the model make it more or less likely to fit the underlying pattern of the data?

title: Impact on Variance
text: Does adding random noise to the model make it more or less sensitive to changes in the training data?
